problem:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=2$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=1+2(x-2)+2(x-2)^{2}+\frac{4}{3}(x-2)^{3}+\frac{2}{3}(x-2)^{4}.
$$

What is ${f}^{‴}(2)?$
worked_solution:
The coefficient of $(x-2)^{3}$ is given by $\frac{{f}^{‴}(2)}{3!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{‴}(2)}{3!} & =\frac{4}{3} \\ \frac{{f}^{‴}(2)}{6} & =\frac{4}{3} \\ {f}^{‴}(2) & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
